title: Common refinement of stratifications and restriction to strata
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme and $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$.

1. Finitely many finite stratifications of $X$ by locally closed subschemes have a common
   refinement which is again a finite stratification by locally closed subschemes; it may
   be chosen so that every stratum is connected and the strata can be ordered
   $S_1,\dots,S_m$ with $S_1\cup\dots\cup S_k$ open in $X$ for every $k$.
2. If $M$ is lisse on a locally closed $S$ and $T\subseteq S$ is locally closed, then $M|_T$
   is lisse. Hence a constructible sheaf is lisse on every stratum of any refinement of a
   stratification adapted to it.
3. For a stratum $g\colon S\to X$, restriction $g^*=g^{-1}$ is exact, and a morphism
   (resp. sequence) of $\Lambda_X$-modules is injective, surjective (resp. exact) iff its
   restriction to every stratum is.

proof.text: Apply [lemma-constructible-common-refinement] successively to the input scheme stratifications: start with the first and refine with the next. Induction on the finite number of inputs gives a common scheme stratification $P_a\to X$: containment of each new image in an earlier image is transitive. For zero input stratifications start with the single stratum $X\to X$; if $X$ is empty use the empty family. Discard empty pieces. Each $P_a\to X$ is an immersion and its image is locally closed by [def-constructible-stratification]. This uses common refinement in its stated sense of containment of images; no factorization morphisms to input strata are asserted.

proof.text:
Write every image $|P_a|=F_a\cap O_a$ with $F_a$ closed and $O_a$ open, and list the finitely many closed sets $F_a$ and $X\setminus O_a$ as $Z_1,\ldots,Z_r$ [def-weil-locally-closed-subset]. For $I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ put $A_I=( igcap_{i\in I}Z_i)\setminus igcup_{j
otin I}Z_j$. The nonempty $A_I$ partition $X$, are locally closed, and membership in every $|P_a|$ is constant on each $A_I$; hence each lies in one $|P_a|$. Order the subsets $I$ by increasing cardinality, breaking ties arbitrarily. For a prefix $D$ of this order, $D$ is downward closed under inclusion. Its complement union of atoms is $ igcup_{I
otin D} igcap_{i\in I}Z_i$: a point with membership set $J$ belongs to this union iff some $I
otin D$ satisfies $I\subseteq J$, iff $J
otin D$. This is a finite union of closed sets, so every prefix union of atoms is open. Empty atoms do not affect this calculation.

proof.text: Realize each atom as a scheme stratum without inferring any scheme factorization from image containment. Choose $a$ with $A_I\subseteq|P_a|$. Put $F_I=\bigcap_{i\in I}Z_i$ (with $F_\varnothing=X$) and $O_I=X\setminus\bigcup_{j\notin I}Z_j$. Let $W_I$ be the open subscheme of $P_a$ over $O_I$. The preimage of $F_I$ in $W_I$ is closed; give it the reduced induced closed subscheme structure $Q_I\hookrightarrow W_I$ using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. The immersion $P_a\to X$ is a homeomorphism onto its image by [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion], so $Q_I$ has precisely image $|P_a|\cap F_I\cap O_I=A_I$. Its composite $Q_I\hookrightarrow W_I\hookrightarrow P_a\to X$ is an immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (e). Thus the $Q_I$ are genuine scheme strata refining every input partition, even if its original strata were nonreduced.

source.place: Tag 01J3 (lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme), Tags 01IO/01HE (immersion definitions), and Tag 02V0 (lemma-composition-immersion); reduced closed subschemes inside open subschemes of P_a

proof.text: For each $A_I=F_I\cap O_I$, the open subscheme $O_I$ of the Noetherian scheme $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Apply [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components] to its closed subset $A_I$: write $A_I=\bigcup_{h=1}^t C_h$ with $C_h$ irreducible and closed in $A_I$. Form the finite graph whose vertices are these $C_h$ and whose edges mean nonempty intersection. Each graph-component union $B$ is connected: irreducibility implies connectedness, and adjoining connected sets meeting the previous union preserves connectedness, since a separation would separate one of the sets. Distinct such unions are disjoint and closed, so each is also open in $A_I$. They cover $A_I$ and are its connected components [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Their inverse images in $Q_I$ are open subschemes, so restricting its immersion gives connected locally closed scheme strata that still refine all original partitions. List these components consecutively in place of each ordered atom. If $V$ is the union of earlier atoms, both $V$ and $V\cup A_I$ are open by step 2. For any union $B$ of components of $A_I$, the complement of $V\cup B$ in $V\cup A_I$ is $A_I\setminus B$, closed there because $A_I$ is closed there and its components are clopen. Therefore $V\cup B$ is open in $X$. This proves all of clause (1), including connectedness and every intermediate prefix.

source.place: (1), connected-component refinement; finite graph argument and preservation of the open-prefix order

proof.text: Let $f:T\to S$ be the actual locally closed inclusion in (2). Lisse means pro-etale locally finite free. Choose a trivializing pro-etale covering $U_i\to S$. Base change gives a covering $T\times_SU_i\to T$ by the covering-preservation assertion of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. By [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], module pullback is the exact inverse image, takes $\Lambda_S$ to $\Lambda_T$, and preserves finite direct sums: the images of the biproduct inclusions and projections satisfy the same identities. Consequently pulling back $M|_{U_i}\simeq\Lambda_{U_i}^{n_i}$ gives $(M|_T)|_{T\times_SU_i}\simeq\Lambda_{T\times_SU_i}^{n_i}$. This proves the first assertion of (2), and the same calculation proves lisse preservation under any scheme morphism. The finite constant models of a constructible sheaf in [sk-def-sfb-constructible] are finite free for the present coefficients: $\Lambda(*)=E$ or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ is a field, so a finitely presented scalar module $P_i$ has a finite basis and $\Lambda_{U_i}\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}P_i\simeq\Lambda_{U_i}^{n_i}$. These are the pulled-back condensed coefficient sheaves, throughout.

source.place: (2), pullback of a trivializing covering and finite free local models

proof.text: For the final assertion of (2), let $i:S\to X$ be an adapted stratum and $j:T\to X$ any refined stratum with $|T|\subseteq|S|$ [def-constructible-refines]. There need not be a morphism $T\to S$. Instead put $W=T\times_XS$ with projections $p:W\to T$ and $q:W\to S$. The map $p$ is an immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft] and is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points]: an immersion induces isomorphic residue fields, since an open immersion preserves local rings and on a closed immersion $A\to A/J$ the residue field at $\mathfrak p/J$ is that at $\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]; thus over each $t$ the residue-field tensor product is $\kappa(t)\otimes_{\kappa(j(t))}\kappa(j(t))=\kappa(t)$, with prime $(0)$. A surjective immersion is closed: in its factorization as closed into an open, surjectivity forces that open to be all of $T$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. By step 5, $p^*j^*M=q^*i^*M$ is lisse. Choose a trivializing covering $C$ of $W$. Apply [new-lem-weil-pbc-proetale-surjective-closed-cover-refinement] to obtain a pro-etale covering $B_b\to T$ such that $W_b=B_b\times_TW$ maps to one member $C_{a(b)}$ of $C$ over $W$. The map $p_b:W_b\to B_b$ is again a surjective closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-closed-immersion-universal-homeomorphism]. On $W_b$ the pullback of $(j^*M)|_{B_b}$ is therefore $\Lambda_{W_b}^{n_{a(b)}}$, also the pullback of $\Lambda_{B_b}^{n_{a(b)}}$ by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. The module inverse image along $p_b$ is an equivalence for every commutative condensed coefficient ring by [new-lem-weil-pbc-condensed-surjective-closed-equivalence]. Fullness lifts this isomorphism and its inverse to $B_b$, and faithfulness makes their composites identities. Hence $(j^*M)|_{B_b}\simeq\Lambda_{B_b}^{n_{a(b)}}$. The covering $B$ proves $j^*M$ lisse. This applies to every refined stratum with its given scheme structure, proving the assertion for any refinement.

proof.text: For every stratum $g:S\to X$, [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] gives $g^*=g^{-1}$ exact on coefficient modules. Use the sheaf clause of [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-stratum-detection] with the identity covering of each stratum and the underlying abelian sheaf: a module with zero restrictions is zero. Exactness identifies restrictions of a kernel or cokernel with the corresponding kernel or cokernel of the restricted morphism, so injectivity and surjectivity are detected; the converses follow by exactness. More explicitly for a sequence $A\xrightarrow a B\xrightarrow b C$, if its restrictions are exact, then every restriction of $\operatorname{im}(ba)$ is zero. Images are kernels of cokernels, so exact pullback preserves them, and detection gives $ba=0$. Now form $H=\ker b/\operatorname{im}a$. Exact pullback identifies its restrictions with the zero homology modules of the restricted sequences, hence detection gives $H=0$, which is exactness at $B$. Apply this argument at each term for a longer sequence. Conversely exact pullback preserves every exact sequence. This proves (3) for any finite stratification, without requiring it to have the order constructed in (1).

source.place: (3), exact inverse image and finite-stratum detection; explicit image and homology calculation
